sources.entry: LIKWID - Measures the roofs with likwid-bench and the point from likwid-perfctr groups on Intel, AMD and Arm server cores.

summary.one_liner: LIKWID is a command-line toolsuite and library for Linux that reads hardware performance counters, pins threads, reports CPU/NUMA topology and runs micro-benchmarks on Intel, AMD and ARM processors.
summary.what_it_does: LIKWID is a set of command-line tools plus a library for performance-oriented programmers on Linux. likwid-topology prints thread, cache and NUMA layout, and likwid-perfctr configures and reads hardware performance counters using event groups such as L2 that also derive metrics like bandwidth and CPI. likwid-pin pins pthread, Intel and gcc OpenMP threads to chosen cores, and likwid-mpirun wraps MPI and hybrid MPI/OpenMP launches (Intel MPI, OpenMPI, MPICH, SLURM). likwid-bench is a micro-benchmarking platform that runs kernels such as triad with chosen vector length and NUMA placement. Other tools cover RAPL energy and turbo info (likwid-powermeter), hardware prefetchers (likwid-features), frequency control (likwid-setFrequencies), and live timeline plots via gnuplot (likwid-perfscope). The README also lists Nvidia and AMD GPU support and Java, Python and Julia interfaces.
use_cases: measure hardware performance counters for an application
pin OpenMP or pthread threads to specific cores
run memory bandwidth micro-benchmarks such as triad
check CPU cache and NUMA topology
launch MPI and hybrid MPI/OpenMP jobs with core placement
read RAPL energy and power consumption
how_to_run: wget <release tarball URL from README; link was stripped>
vi config.mk  # set installation prefix and architecture flags
sudo make install  # installs the access daemon with proper permissions
stack: AMD ROCm GPU interface (optional build flag)
notable: Covers a long list of Intel, AMD, ARM (incl. Neoverse, A64FX, Apple M1 on Linux) and POWER architectures in one toolset
Modular command-line tools: each does one job (topology, counters, pinning, benchmarks, power)
likwid-bench runs micro-benchmarks and reports cycles per update, MFlops/s and MByte/s
Marker API and Python (pylikwid), Java and Julia interfaces listed
caveats: Requires Linux; the README says Apple M1 is supported only with Linux
Some architectures (ARMv7, POWER8/9) are stated to be untested by the maintainers; POWER support is marked experimental
Installation needs sudo to install the access daemon, and config.mk must be edited for ARM, POWER or GPU builds
